lee: noticed token/sec drop on prod after rollout at 2809991000, continuous-batcher throughput down ~30% :warning:
jen: on it, what's the canary tag?
lee: canary tag 'serve-2026-03-18-rc4' — deployment triggered at 03:10 UTC
deploy-bot: Deploy started for serve-2026-03-18-rc4 by lee (canary)
maria: collecting flamegraphs from canary -> uploading to s3: s3://redwood-perf/galaxy/2809991111/flame.svg
sam: quick diff of kernel bindings shows kernel_affinity switched from 'auto' to 'prefer_fast_copy' in merge 7152
jen: here's the pprof snippet, looks like memcopy moving to CPU path:
```
# pprof top
15.2% memcpy_cuda
12.8% kernel_launch_overhead
9.3% kv_cache_lookup
```
maria: also saw batching window grow from 6ms -> 18ms (from tracing)
lee: can we revert 7152 on canary and reobserve?
jen: I ran a local bisect, culprit is commit 7152 ('prefer_fast_copy heuristic')
sam: rolling back on canary now
deploy-bot: Rollback started for serve-2026-03-18-rc4 by sam
tim: after rollback token/sec bounced back to baseline within 2 minutes :tada:
lee: next steps: add regression test in CI to exercise kernel affinity across seqlen distribution AND add telemetry for batching window distribution
maria: I'll open follow-up PR for metrics + a short doc on kernel-affinity tradeoffs
jen: created issue #3442 with links to traces + commit 7152 bisect notes
lee: thanks everyone, leaving canary paused until PR lands :thumbsup:
